area: mobile first run and connection - main.dart connection screen, mobile_discovery_ops, qr_scanner_screen, saved_servers_screen, tailscale_setup_sheet, first_run_setup_screen, checkpoint_resume_dialog

units_unreached.why: FirstRunSetupScreen is only mounted by mobile_dashboard_screen.dart:96 when shouldRunFirstRunSetupProvider resolves to setupNeeds.hasAnyMissing, which requires a live NetworkBackend session against a paired host whose /api/info reports a missing image output path, missing catalogs or no equipment profile. With no appliance paired the gate never renders it. I did reach the shell via 'Skip Connection (View UI Only)', but that path lands in the SHARED 13-step wizard (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/onboarding/onboarding_screen.dart), not this file - confirmed by the on-screen title 'Set up your rig / Step 1 of 13', which exists only in onboarding_screen.dart:736, whereas first_run_setup_screen.dart has three steps (output path, catalogs, profiles). The one appliance reachable from this emulator is another agent's live desktop instance on the host at 10.0.2.2:8391, and pairing with it would both violate the no-appliance premise of this sweep and disturb a concurrent audit.

Shown only from _checkForCheckpoint (mobile_reconnect_ops.dart:552-583), which runs once after a connection is established and returns early unless executor.getCheckpointInfo() yields a checkpoint with canResume == true - i.e. it needs a host with a sequence run that was interrupted mid-flight. Unreachable with no appliance and no prior run. Source read only: the dialog itself is a pure presentation widget over CheckpointInfo with Discard/Resume actions and no network calls, and its caller already loops until resume-or-discard succeeds rather than stranding the checkpoint.

findings.title: An unreachable host is reported as 'the server did not report a valid API version - update the server', blaming software that is fine
findings.what_happened: Connect over Tailscale with a MagicDNS name that does not exist. After ~3s the sheet closes and the connection screen error slot reads: 'The Skotiq server did not report a valid API version. Update the server before connecting.' Nothing was ever reached - the name does not resolve. The message names the wrong subsystem, prescribes the wrong fix (go update the observatory PC), and omits the host, the URL and the real cause.
findings.expected: The same class of message the manual Enter-IP path already produces - 'Cannot reach http://<host>:<port>/api/info from this device' plus the tailnet-specific hint (is Tailscale running on this phone and on the rig, is the MagicDNS name spelled correctly). A version-compatibility verdict must only be rendered when /api/info actually answered.
findings.repro: Connection screen -> Connect over Tailscale -> Tailscale address = skotiq-rig.tail1a2b3.ts.net, Port 8080, Transport HTTP -> Connect.
findings.evidence: Ground truth on the host: `getent hosts skotiq-rig.tail1a2b3.ts.net` exits 2 (no record) and `curl http://skotiq-rig.tail1a2b3.ts.net:8080/api/info` returns 'curl: (6) Could not resolve host'. App a11y tree 3s after Connect, unchanged through 37s of polling: View[121,482][959,577] 'The Skotiq server did not report a valid API version. Update the server before connecting.' Mechanism: _connectToServer calls EnhancedSkotiqDiscovery.fetchServerInfo, which returns null on ANY network failure; the code then keeps the synthetic DiscoveredServer (apiVersion and version both null) and passes that null into SkotiqServerCompatibility.check, whose null branch is exactly this string. Every entry point that routes through _connectToServer with an unreachable host - Tailscale sheet, QR payload, saved-server row - gets the same wrong diagnosis. Only the manual Enter-IP form, which has its own reachability pre-flight, tells the truth.
findings.proposed_fix: In _connectToServer, distinguish 'fetchServerInfo returned null' (unreachable / not a Skotiq endpoint) from 'fetchServerInfo answered but the version is unparseable'. Only run SkotiqServerCompatibility.check on the fetched-and-parsed case; on null, emit the reachability message that already exists on the manual path, parameterised by scheme/host/port.

findings.title: Mobile onboarding decides ASCOM is unavailable from the PHONE's OS, so a phone paired to a Windows rig can never pick ASCOM
findings.what_happened: The driver-selection step offers Native / Alpaca / INDI / Sim and prints 'ASCOM COM drivers are Windows-only. Use Alpaca to reach an ASCOM server from this platform.' The available-driver set is computed from Platform.isWindows - the platform of the DEVICE RUNNING THE UI. On Android that is false by construction, so the ASCOM tile can never be offered on the phone, no matter what the host is. Drivers run on the host, not on the phone, and the host already publishes the correct answer: /api/info returns platformCapabilities.drivers[] with backend 'ascom', status and supportedPlatforms.
findings.expected: Drive the driver list from the connected host's platformCapabilities (already served by /api/info), falling back to the local platform only when this device IS the backend. On a phone paired to a Windows imaging PC, ASCOM must be offered and the Windows-only footnote must not appear.
findings.repro: Connection screen -> 'Skip Connection (View UI Only)' -> Next -> Step 2 of 13 'Drivers'.
findings.evidence: Observed on the emulator: driver tiles are exactly 'Native', 'Alpaca', 'INDI', 'Sim' and the footnote 'ASCOM COM drivers are Windows-only. Use Alpaca to reach an ASCOM server from this platform.' is present. Source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/onboarding_provider.dart:73-84 adds DriverType.ascom only `if (Platform.isWindows)`; driver_step.dart:58 renders the footnote whenever the set lacks ascom. Host /api/info (curl http://127.0.0.1:8391/api/info) does carry the right signal: platformCapabilities.drivers[] includes {"backend":"ascom","label":"ASCOM COM","status":"unsupported","supportedPlatforms":["windows"]}. SOURCE-ONLY for the specific claim 'still hidden when the host is Windows': I could not pair with a Windows host from this emulator, but Platform.isWindows is false on Android by definition, so the tile cannot appear regardless of host.

findings.title: With no network at all (airplane mode) the app still blames the network it is not on, and tells the user to open firewall ports
findings.what_happened: In airplane mode the launch discovery fails and the app shows the identical LAN-failure card: 'No Skotiq server found on this network... use "Connect over Tailscale"... On the same network, try: scanning the QR code from the desktop / entering the host address manually / allowing UDP 45679 and HTTP 8080 through the firewall.' The phone has no network at all, so there is no 'this network', Tailscale cannot work either, and nothing about the observatory PC's firewall is relevant. A first-timer in the field is sent to reconfigure a firewall to fix airplane mode.
findings.expected: Check connectivity before blaming the LAN: 'This phone has no network connection - turn off Airplane mode or join the observatory's Wi-Fi.' Only fall through to the firewall/QR/manual advice when the device actually has a network.
findings.repro: adb shell cmd connectivity airplane-mode enable; force-stop and relaunch the app; read the error card.
findings.evidence: a11y tree with airplane mode on: View[121,482][959,955] 'No Skotiq server found on this network. ~ If you are away from the observatory, use "Connect over Tailscale" to reach it by its MagicDNS name - local discovery only works on the same WiFi. ~ On the same network, try: - Scanning the QR code from the desktop - Entering the host address manually - Allowing UDP 45679 and HTTP 8080 through the firewall'. Identical string to the with-network no-server case. The error text is a single hardcoded literal at mobile_discovery_ops.dart:53-61 with no connectivity branch.

findings.title: Discovery never retries when the phone regains connectivity; the stale failure card sits there indefinitely
findings.what_happened: After a failed discovery the connection screen keeps its failure card forever. Turning the network back on changes nothing: 46s after Wi-Fi came back and validated, the screen still read 'No Skotiq server found on this network'. One manual tap on 'Search for Server' then found the appliance in about 10s. On a phone, 'the network just changed' is the single most likely reason the last failure is stale - walking into the observatory's Wi-Fi, coming off airplane mode, roaming from cellular.
findings.expected: Subscribe to connectivity changes on the connection screen and re-run discovery automatically when a network becomes available (with the existing 'Searching...' status so it is visible), or at minimum surface a 'Network changed - tap to rescan' affordance.
findings.repro: airplane-mode enable -> relaunch -> discovery fails -> airplane-mode disable -> wait, touching nothing.
findings.evidence: adb dumpsys connectivity shows WIFI network{103} CONNECTED/IS_VALIDATED at T+6s (firstValidated recorded). App a11y tree sampled at T+6/14/22/30/38/46s is byte-identical, still showing the no-server card and no 'Searching' status. Immediately afterwards, tapping 'Search for Server' produced 'Searching via network broadcast...' and reached the appliance (pairing dialog for http://10.0.2.2:8391) about 10s later - so the network path was working the whole time.
findings.where: apps/mobile/lib/main_parts/mobile_discovery_ops.dart:_autoConnect (called once from initState; no connectivity listener on the connection screen)

findings.title: System Back on the connection screen quits the app instead of closing the manual-entry form
findings.what_happened: On the first-run connection screen, 'Enter IP' replaces the option list with an inline Server address / Access Token form. One Back press dismisses the keyboard; the next terminates the app to the launcher. The typed server address is lost.
findings.expected: Back should close the manual-entry form and restore the connection-option list. Only a Back press with the option list already showing should be able to leave the app - and this is precisely the shell PopScope treatment the main app shell already has.
findings.repro: Fresh install, no host. Tap 'Enter IP', type 192.0.2.77, Connect, wait for the error. Press Back (IME closes). Press Back again.
findings.evidence: adb dumpsys window after the second Back: mCurrentFocus=Window{... com.google.android.apps.nexuslauncher/...NexusLauncherActivity}; the a11y tree is the Android home screen (At a glance / Gmail / Photos). Relaunching returns to the option list with the typed address gone.
findings.where: apps/mobile/lib/main.dart (connection-screen MaterialApp; the manual-entry state has no PopScope)

findings.title: Saved servers empty state tells the user to pair with the 'Add server' button, which only closes the screen
findings.what_happened: With no saved servers the screen shows 'No saved servers yet' / 'Pair with a Skotiq host using the "Add server" button to start the roaming list.' Tapping the Add server FAB pops the screen back to the connection screen with no snackbar, no dialog and no explanation. Nothing is added and nothing says why. From the user's side the button looks broken.
findings.expected: Either the FAB opens an add/pair flow as its label and the empty-state copy promise, or the empty state names the real path ('Servers are saved automatically once a connection succeeds - connect from the previous screen') and the FAB is relabelled or removed.
findings.repro: Connection screen -> 'Saved servers' -> read the empty state -> tap 'Add server'.
findings.evidence: a11y tree before: 'No saved servers yet' + 'Pair with a Skotiq host using the "Add server" button to start the roaming list.' + Button 'Add server' [695,2148][1038,2295]. After the tap the tree is the connection screen again and the list is untouched. Source confirms it is deliberate: onAddServer is wired to `Navigator.of(screenContext).pop(); return null;` (mobile_discovery_ops.dart:269-272) and the null return is documented as suppressing the snackbar (saved_servers_screen.dart:406-414).

findings.title: QR scanner keeps claiming 'Camera permission is required' after the user grants it in the settings page the app itself opened
findings.what_happened: Deny camera twice and the scanner correctly shows 'Camera permission is required to scan pairing QR codes' plus an 'Open settings' button. Tapping it opens Android's app-info page for Skotiq. Granting Camera there and pressing Back returns to the scanner, which STILL shows the same message and no preview. The permission IS granted - one tap on 'Retry camera' starts the preview instantly.
findings.expected: Re-check the permission on app resume (didChangeAppLifecycleState -> resumed) and start the preview automatically. The app sent the user to settings to do exactly this; the flow it prescribes must not dead-end on return.
findings.repro: adb shell pm revoke com.skotiq.mobile android.permission.CAMERA; relaunch; Cancel the pairing dialog; 'Scan QR'; Deny; 'Retry camera'; Deny -> 'Open settings' appears; tap it; grant Camera; press Back.
findings.evidence: After Back, mCurrentFocus=com.skotiq.mobile/...MainActivity and the tree is still 'Camera permission is required to scan pairing QR codes. Allow camera access for Skotiq, then retry.' + Retry camera + Open settings. One tap on 'Retry camera' then yields the live scanner tree (Toggle torch, 'No second camera available').
findings.where: apps/mobile/lib/screens/qr_scanner_screen.dart (permission state refreshed only by the explicit Retry action; no WidgetsBindingObserver)

findings.title: Relay dialog throws away both typed fields on every validation failure
findings.what_happened: 'Connect via Relay' opens a dialog with a relay URL and an appliance id. Any validation failure - both blank, or an appliance id that is not xxxx-xxxx-xxxx - CLOSES the dialog and prints the validation text on the connection screen behind it. Both fields are destroyed, so a mistyped 14-character appliance id costs a full re-entry of a long https relay URL as well. The Tailscale sheet, in contrast, validates inline and stays open.
findings.expected: Validate inline inside the dialog and keep it open with the entered values, exactly as tailscale_setup_sheet does ('Enter the rig's Tailscale name or IP' renders under the field with the sheet still up). Also show the xxxx-xxxx-xxxx format as field hint text rather than only after a failure.
findings.repro: Connect via Relay -> tap Connect with both fields blank -> dialog closes, 'Enter both a relay URL and an appliance id.' appears behind it. Reopen, type https://relay.tail1a2b3.invalid and appliance id 'abc123' -> Connect -> dialog closes, 'Appliance id must look like xxxx-xxxx-xxxx.' and both fields are gone.
findings.evidence: Both cases observed; after each failure the a11y tree is the connection screen (Enter IP / Scan QR / Connect over Tailscale / ... buttons) with the message in the error slot at [121,482], and reopening the dialog shows two empty EditTexts at [168,1091][912,1217] and [168,1238][912,1364].
findings.where: apps/mobile/lib/main_parts/mobile_discovery_ops.dart:_showRelayConnectDialog (validation is performed by the caller after the dialog resolves, not inside it)

findings.title: Tailscale sheet throws away the typed MagicDNS name on every failed connect
findings.what_happened: On a failed connect the sheet closes and the entered Tailscale address is discarded. Reopening 'Connect over Tailscale' shows an empty address field. A MagicDNS name is ~30 characters ('skotiq-rig.tail1a2b3.ts.net') and has to be retyped in full on a phone keyboard for every retry - in the dark, next to a rig.
findings.expected: Keep the sheet open on failure with the address preserved and the error inline (the blank-address validation already renders inline correctly), or persist the last-entered tailnet host and prefill it - which the relay dialog already does from the saved-servers store.
findings.repro: Connect over Tailscale -> type skotiq-rig.tail1a2b3.ts.net -> Connect -> (fails) -> tap 'Connect over Tailscale' again.
findings.evidence: EditTexts after reopening: [63,1508][1017,1634] text='' (address), [63,1723][378,1849] text='8080' (port), [63,1938][1017,2127] text='' (token). Contrast mobile_discovery_ops.dart:184-196, where the relay dialog explicitly prefills relayUrl/applianceId from savedServersServiceProvider.

findings.title: 'Skip Connection (View UI Only)' drops the user into a hardware setup wizard that blames their unplugged camera instead of the missing server
findings.what_happened: The escape hatch labelled 'View UI Only' does not show the UI - it opens the 13-step 'Set up your rig' wizard. Step 3 (Camera) says 'No devices found. Make sure your device is connected and powered on, then try Scan again.' There is no server to scan from; the phone is deliberately in UI-only mode. Tapping 'Scan again' produces no spinner, no error and no change - a silent no-op, verified across 17s of polling and an empty app logcat. 'Next' then refuses to advance: 'Pick a camera to continue, or use "Skip onboarding" to set it up later.' The only way forward is 'Skip onboarding'.
findings.expected: In UI-only mode either skip the rig wizard entirely and go straight to the shell (which is what the label promises and what the user gets after Skip onboarding anyway), or have the discovery steps say the true thing - 'Not connected to a Skotiq server, so nothing can be scanned' - rather than blaming the user's hardware. Note first_run_setup_screen.dart already gets this right: its bootstrap sets the error string 'The phone is not connected to a server.' when the backend is not a NetworkBackend.
findings.repro: Connection screen -> 'Skip Connection (View UI Only)' -> Next -> Next -> Step 3 of 13 'Camera' -> 'Scan again'.
findings.evidence: a11y tree at step 3: 'No devices found. Make sure your device is connected and powered on, then try Scan again.' with tabs 'Native (0) / Alpaca / INDI'. Three consecutive dumps at t=5s/11s/17s after tapping 'Scan again' are identical; `adb logcat | grep flutter` is empty over the same window. Tapping Next leaves 'Step 3 of 13' and adds 'Pick a camera to continue, or use "Skip onboarding" to set it up later.'

findings.title: Two onboarding prompts are presented at the same time on the first dashboard
findings.what_happened: After 'Skip onboarding' the dashboard renders with the modal 'Welcome to Skotiq - Step 1 of 7' tour card (Skip - I know what I'm doing / Show me around) AND, simultaneously, a 'Dashboard Tour - Learn about the dashboard controls and status displays' card with its own Maybe Later / Start Tour buttons. Both are live in the accessibility tree at once, so a screen reader reads two competing tour offers, and sighted users see a dimmed second offer behind the first.
findings.expected: One onboarding prompt at a time. The dashboard tour card should be suppressed while the app-level tour overlay is up (and ideally only offered after it is dismissed).
findings.repro: Skip Connection (View UI Only) -> Skip onboarding -> look at the dashboard.
findings.evidence: Single a11y dump contains both: 'Onboarding tour: Welcome to Skotiq ~ Step 1 of 7 ...' with Buttons 'Skip - I know what I'm doing' [97,1326][510,1452] and 'Show me around' [531,1326][842,1452], and 'Dashboard Tour' [442,1597][1004,1744] with Buttons 'Maybe Later' [442,1775][756,1901] and 'Start Tour' [777,1775][1004,1901]. Screenshot /tmp/ns-android/shots/07-uionly-dash.png shows the second card dimmed behind the first.

findings.title: The onboarding tour announces keyboard shortcuts that do not exist on a phone
findings.what_happened: The tour overlay's accessibility label on Android reads 'Skotiq onboarding tour, step 1 of 7, Press Enter for next step, Backspace for previous, Escape to skip'. A phone has no Enter, Backspace or Escape key; a TalkBack user is given three instructions none of which they can follow, and the actual gesture (activate the on-screen buttons) is never mentioned.
findings.expected: Platform-conditional label: keep the key hints on desktop, and on touch platforms announce the buttons ('double-tap Show me around to continue, Skip to dismiss').
findings.repro: Skip Connection (View UI Only) -> Skip onboarding -> dump the accessibility tree.
findings.evidence: Root a11y node [0,0][1080,2400] content-desc: 'Skotiq onboarding tour, step 1 of 7, Press Enter for next step, Backspace for previous, Escape to skip'.

findings.title: 'Retry camera' is a dead control once the permission is permanently denied
findings.what_happened: After two denials Android stops showing the permission dialog. 'Retry camera' stays enabled; tapping it produces no dialog, no snackbar and no text change - the screen is identical before and after. The app knows the state, because this is exactly when it adds the 'Open settings' button, yet it keeps offering a button that cannot succeed.
findings.expected: Once 'Open settings' has appeared, either disable 'Retry camera' with a reason or change it to say 'Camera access is blocked in Android settings - use Open settings'. A control that cannot do anything must not look identical to one that can.
findings.repro: Scan QR -> Deny -> Retry camera -> Deny -> ('Open settings' appears) -> tap 'Retry camera'.
findings.evidence: Two a11y dumps around the tap are identical: 'Camera permission is required...' + Button 'Retry camera' [240,1252][525,1378] + Button 'Open settings' [546,1252][840,1378]; no app logcat output.

findings.title: QR scanner close (X) button has no accessibility label
findings.what_happened: The AppBar leading IconButton (Icons.close) is the only way out of the fullscreen scanner besides system Back, and it exposes an empty content-desc, so a screen reader announces an unlabelled button. Every other control on the screen is labelled ('Toggle torch', 'No second camera available'), and the Saved-servers screen's back arrow is labelled 'Back'.
findings.expected: tooltip: 'Close' (or a Semantics label), matching the rest of the app.
findings.repro: Connection screen -> Scan QR -> dump the view hierarchy.
findings.evidence: uiautomator node: clickable Button [11,139][137,265] with text='' and content-desc=''. Source: apps/mobile/lib/screens/qr_scanner_screen.dart:296-299, IconButton(icon: Icon(Icons.close), onPressed: ...) with no tooltip.

findings.title: Transport segmented control exposes no selected state to accessibility
findings.what_happened: The HTTP / HTTPS transport selector renders HTTP as the selected chip, but in the accessibility tree only the UNSELECTED option ('HTTPS') is a node at all, and it reports selected=false, checked=false. The currently selected value is a plain non-interactive View. A screen-reader user cannot tell which transport is active, and cannot discover that the visible highlighted chip is the current choice.
findings.expected: Both segments should be semantics nodes with inSelectedState / selected true-false, as the design system's other toggle rows do (the sheet's own 'Trust self-signed relay TLS' checkbox correctly reports off).
findings.repro: Connect over Tailscale -> dump the view hierarchy and inspect the Transport row.
findings.evidence: Nodes: non-clickable View [526,1754][608,1796] 'HTTP' (the selected one), clickable [713,1733][1007,1817] 'HTTPS' selected=false checked=false. Screenshot /tmp/ns-android/shots/06-tailscale.png shows HTTP highlighted.

findings.title: Three entry points, three different vocabularies for the same failure - one of them raw Dart exception text
findings.what_happened: The same underlying condition - 'the address you gave me does not answer' - is reported three different ways depending on which button the user pressed. Enter IP: 'Cannot reach http://192.0.2.77:8080/api/info from this device.' followed by two well-written paragraphs of what to check on the PC and on the phone. Relay: 'Could not reach the relay: SocketException: Failed host lookup: \'relay.tail1a2b3.invalid\' (OS Error: No address associated with hostname, errno = 7)'. Tailscale: the wrong message entirely (see the P1 above). The relay text leaks a Dart exception class, an OS error string and an errno onto a consumer screen at 2am.
findings.expected: One shared reachability-failure renderer used by every entry point: what was tried (scheme://host:port/api/info), the plain-language cause (name not found / connection refused / timed out), and the next step. The Enter-IP copy is already the right answer - promote it and delete the other two paths' bespoke strings.
findings.repro: Compare Enter IP -> 192.0.2.77 -> Connect, Connect via Relay -> https://relay.tail1a2b3.invalid + abcd-efgh-ijkl -> Connect, and Connect over Tailscale -> skotiq-rig.tail1a2b3.ts.net -> Connect.
findings.evidence: Verbatim a11y strings captured for all three, listed above; each observed on the emulator with no appliance at the given address.

findings.title: After discovery has already failed, the biggest button on screen re-runs the thing that just failed
findings.what_happened: The connection screen offers seven actions. Six are equally-weighted low-contrast text buttons (Enter IP 209x126px, Scan QR 216x126px, Connect over Tailscale, Connect via Relay, Saved servers, Skip Connection) and exactly one is a filled primary button: 'Search for Server' (996x131px), which repeats the automatic discovery that ran on launch and failed 4 seconds ago. The action with the highest success probability for someone standing next to their rig - Scan QR, because the desktop puts a QR on screen when you start pairing - is a small text button, and the error card that lists 'Scanning the QR code from the desktop' as the first thing to try offers no button to do it.
findings.expected: Once discovery has failed at least once, promote 'Scan QR' to the primary filled button and demote 'Search for Server' to a text action ('Scan again'). Better still, make the three bullets in the failure card tappable so 'Scanning the QR code from the desktop' opens the scanner directly - that removes a full step from the most likely recovery path.
findings.repro: Launch with no appliance, wait for the failure card, count the actions and their weights.
findings.evidence: Measured bounds at 420dpi (2.625 px/dp): Enter IP [317,1076][526,1202], Scan QR [547,1076][763,1202], Connect over Tailscale [339,1223][741,1349], Connect via Relay [370,1370][710,1496], Saved servers [395,1517][685,1643], Search for Server [42,1643][1038,1774] (the only filled one), Skip Connection [42,1805][1038,1931]. Screenshot /tmp/ns-android/shots/02-firstrun.png.

findings.title: The Tailscale sheet tells the user to go install an app but will not take them there, and never checks whether it is already installed
findings.what_happened: Step 1 of the sheet reads 'Install Tailscale on this phone - Get it from the App Store / Play Store and sign in with the same account as your observatory PC.' It is plain text: nothing is tappable, so the user must leave Skotiq, find the store, search for Tailscale, install, sign in, and come back and retype everything (which the sheet then discards on the next failure). The sheet also never checks whether Tailscale is present or up on this phone, even though that is trivially detectable on Android and is the single most common reason the connect will fail.
findings.expected: On a phone this should be a button that deep-links to the Play Store listing (market://details?id=com.tailscale.ipn), and step 1 should collapse to a green tick when the package is already installed. Detecting 'Tailscale is not installed' before the connect attempt turns a mystery timeout into a one-line answer.
findings.repro: Connection screen -> Connect over Tailscale -> read step 1; nothing in it is a control.
findings.evidence: a11y tree: 'Install Tailscale on this phone' [276,765][972,820] and 'Get it from the App Store / Play Store and sign in with the same account as your observatory PC.' [213,825][972,920] are both non-clickable Views; the only clickable nodes in the sheet are Close, the three inputs, the HTTPS chip, Cancel and Connect.

findings.title: Manual entry asks for an 'Access Token' that a first-time user cannot have, and never mentions the port it will use
findings.what_happened: The Enter-IP form has exactly two fields: 'Server address' and 'Access Token' (with a show/hide eye). A first-run user has no access token - the real first-connect credential is the pairing CODE, which the app asks for afterwards in its own dialog. There is no helper text saying the token is optional, and no hint that the address may include a port or that 8080 is assumed; the user only learns the port from the failure message afterwards ('Cannot reach http://192.0.2.77:8080/api/info').
findings.expected: Label it 'Access token (optional - leave blank to pair with a code)', exactly the phrasing the Tailscale sheet already uses for the same field ('Leave blank to pair with a code'), and give the address field the hint '192.168.1.20 or 192.168.1.20:8080 (default 8080)'.
findings.repro: Connection screen -> Enter IP -> inspect the two fields.
findings.evidence: Screenshot /tmp/ns-android/shots/03-enterip.png: fields are hinted only 'Server address' and 'Access Token'. Compare /tmp/ns-android/shots/06-tailscale.png, where the same field is labelled 'Access token (optional)' with hint 'Leave blank to pair with a code'.

verified_correct: Manual Enter-IP failure is honest, fast and genuinely actionable. Attack: 192.0.2.77 (RFC5737 TEST-NET, guaranteed unroutable). In about 4s the app produced 'Cannot reach http://192.0.2.77:8080/api/info from this device.' + 'On the computer running Skotiq: confirm Settings -> Remote Access shows "Running" (on a headless appliance, that the service is up), note the LAN URL, and allow port 8080 through that machine's firewall on the private/local network.' + 'On this device: open that URL in a browser - you should see JSON. Then try Connect again or scan the QR after starting pairing.' It names the exact URL it tried, gives a verification step the user can perform independently, and did not hang (state stable and unchanged from t=6s through t=46s).

Discovery does not hang and does not silently pretend. 'Search for Server' shows 'Searching via Bonjour...' then 'Searching via network broadcast...' and terminates. Cascade measured: mDNS registered a _skotiq._tcp listener at 16:43:18.896 and unregistered it at 16:43:21.946 (3.05s, matching the coded 3s budget) per the system serviceDiscovery log, then the UDP stage runs. When a server IS present the broadcast stage found it in about 10s end to end.

The failure copy's port numbers are correct, not decorative. 'Allowing UDP 45679 and HTTP 8080 through the firewall' matches SkotiqDiscovery._discoveryPort = 45679 (packages/skotiq_remote_protocol/lib/src/discovery.dart:535, secure_discovery.dart:75) and the host's actual web port.

A failed connection attempt does NOT create a phantom saved server. After the 192.0.2.77 failure, 'Saved servers' still showed 'No saved servers yet', and FlutterSharedPreferences.xml contained only the migration flags and the device id - no last-server record. The next launch's 'Connecting to Skotiq Headless...' came from live discovery of a real host (confirmed: `ss -ltnp` shows skotiq_desk listening on 0.0.0.0:8391 and /api/info returns name 'Skotiq Headless'), not from a fabricated saved entry.
A wrong pairing code is rejected plainly: entering 000000 produced 'The pairing code is not recognised.' and returned to the full option list, with no partial or fake 'connected' state.

The QR scanner's camera-switch button is a model disabled control: on a device with one usable camera it is reported DISABLED with the reason as its label ('No second camera available') rather than being enabled and silently failing.

The permanently-denied camera path offers the right escape: after the second denial an 'Open settings' button appears and correctly deep-links to the app's own settings page (mCurrentFocus became com.android.settings/...SpaActivity showing the Skotiq app page).

Empty-field validation in both the Tailscale sheet and the relay dialog states the requirement rather than failing vaguely: 'Enter the rig's Tailscale name or IP' (inline, sheet stays open) and 'Enter both a relay URL and an appliance id.' / 'Appliance id must look like xxxx-xxxx-xxxx.'

The relay failure is truthful about the cause even if the wording is raw: 'Could not reach the relay: SocketException: Failed host lookup: relay.tail1a2b3.invalid' correctly identifies name resolution as the failure - it does not blame the server version the way the Tailscale path does.

The UI-only dashboard's empty states are honest: 'Idle', 'No run active', 'No runs yet - your first night will appear here.', 'Set an observing location to generate target plans.' Nothing was invented to fill the screen with a disconnected backend.

Tap targets on the connection screen meet the 48dp minimum: every action button is 126px tall at 420dpi = exactly 48dp, and the primary is 131px (50dp). Text on the failure card and the How-to-Connect card is legible at arm's length in the dark theme.
coverage_note: Driven live on ns_test_api35 (1080x2400, 420dpi) against a debug build. Harness notes for whoever runs this next: (1) the installed APK initially failed with 'Dart Error: Can't load Kernel binary: Indicated size is invalid' and the app never got past the splash - a full `adb uninstall` followed by `adb install -r -g` fixed it; the on-disk APK was intact (kernel_blob.bin walks 151 valid components), so it was a stale extracted-resource cache from the previous install. (2) drive_android.py tree returns NOTHING until an accessibility service is running, because Flutter only builds a semantics tree when AccessibilityManager is enabled - `adb shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.android.systemui.accessibility.accessibilitymenu/.AccessibilityMenuService` plus `accessibility_enabled 1` makes the whole harness work and does not intercept taps the way TalkBack would. (3) `drive_android.py tap Connect` is dangerous on this screen: substring matching hits 'Not Connected' first and taps the status label instead of the button - use tap-xy from the dumped bounds for anything containing 'connect'. Scope caveat: the sweep was specified as 'no appliance reachable', and that held for the first half, but partway through, a concurrent agent's desktop instance came up on the host at 10.0.2.2:8391 and the app began discovering it; findings above are split accordingly - the unreachable-path findings were all reproduced against addresses that are unroutable or unresolvable by construction (192.0.2.77, *.tail1a2b3.ts.net, *.invalid), verified from the host with getent/curl.
